candidate.rule_context:
COMPLIANCE MEMO - CASH ACCEPTANCE RULES
From: Bridgeport City Attorney's Office, Consumer Protection Unit
Re: Ordinance 14-B-112 cash acceptance requirements for retail storefronts
Date: effective all bot deployments

The rule applies to any retail establishment with a physical storefront in Bridgeport that sells goods or services directly to consumers at that location. The test is functional, not technological: if a customer can walk in and attempt to pay with U.S. currency, the business must have a means to accept and process that payment at the point of sale. 

In scope: all card-primary or mixed-payment POS configurations where the cash drawer and coin handling are active and staffed during all regular business hours, with no minimum threshold or separate-queue requirement that makes cash materially slower or less available than electronic methods. A cash-back-only drawer (debit cash-back, ATM-style) does not satisfy the rule because it requires an electronic transaction first; the rule requires acceptance of cash as a standalone payment method.

Out of scope: online or phone orders with no physical pickup at a staffed register; purely service transactions billed by invoice with no walk-up component; temporary pop-ups under 14 days per separate exemption.

Classification aid: any POS mode that requires the customer to first pay electronically to generate a cash transaction fails the standalone-cash test. Any mode that routes cash customers to a separate line or device with worse hours also fails. Staff must be present and trained; an unmanned cash box does not qualify.

Penalty reference: first violation $250 city fine, escalates per repeat. Bot must not recommend configurations that place the user in violation.

-- M. Deluca, Senior Assistant City Attorney, Consumer Affairs

rules.rule_context:
CASH ACCEPTANCE RULE - PERMANENT BOT DIRECTIVE

Bridgeport Ordinance 14-B-112 requires any retail establishment with a physical storefront in the city to accept U.S. currency as a form of payment when goods or services are sold directly to consumers at that location. This applies to all businesses with a staffed point of sale during regular hours where a customer can walk in and attempt to make a purchase.

The compliance test is functional: cash must be accepted as a standalone payment method at the point of sale, without requiring the customer to first initiate an electronic transaction. A configuration that only dispenses cash as a secondary output of a card or debit transaction does not satisfy this requirement. The rule also requires that cash acceptance be available during the same hours and at the same location as electronic payment, with no separate queue or materially slower process that discourages its use.

The bot must not recommend any POS configuration, payment flow, or operational setup that results in a retail storefront being unable to accept cash directly at the register. Exemptions exist for online-only sales, invoice-based services with no walk-up component, and temporary operations under 14 days per separate ordinance section.

First violation carries a $250 city fine with escalation for repeats.
